question: Which of these is a valid medical reason to put in an indwelling urinary catheter?

options.A: General urinary incontinence with no skin breakdown
options.B: To make things easier for nursing staff during busy night shifts
options.C: Accurate hourly urine output measurement in a critically ill patient
options.D: The patient prefers not to get up to use the toilet at night

explanation: Spot on! We only use indwelling catheters when there is a strong medical need, like closely tracking kidney function in very sick patients.

question: What is the main goal of risk management in nursing?

options.A: Increasing the number of daily patient admissions
options.B: Protecting patients, staff, and facilities from harm
options.C: Punishing staff members who make clinical errors
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital equipment purchases

explanation: You've got this! Risk management is all about keeping everyone in the hospital safe by spotting dangers early and stopping accidents before they happen.

question: How do you measure the correct insertion length for a nasogastric tube?

options.A: From the mouth straight down to the knee
options.B: From the center of the chest to the wrist
options.C: From the forehead down to the belly button
options.D: From nose to earlobe to xiphoid process

explanation: This classic anatomical landmark measurement ensures the tip of the tube reaches safely inside the stomach cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h4)

question: A nurse assumes an older patient with confusion simply has baseline dementia, without checking for a new urinary tract infection. Which cognitive trap is this?

options.A: Sensory overload
options.B: Physical fatigue
options.C: Equipment failure
options.D: Confirmation bias

explanation: That's right! Confirmation bias happens when we lock onto our first impression and stop looking for other possible causes—like a sneaky UTI causing sudden confusion.

question: Why is it helpful for a nurse to assess the nutrition of an entire family rather than just one person?

options.A: Family members always have identical nutritional requirements
options.B: Individual assessments are legally prohibited in community clinics
options.C: Hospital policies require whole-family admission for dietary advice
options.D: Families usually share similar eating habits and money challenges

explanation: Looking at the whole family helps you see the big picture—like what kind of food is cooked at home and what challenges everyone faces together.

question: Why is modern healthcare now encouraging fathers to get involved during pregnancy?

options.A: Government policies now fine fathers who stay away.
options.B: Women are no longer able to attend clinics alone.
options.C: Shared decision-making improves overall health outcomes.
options.D: Hospitals have extra space to accommodate couples.

explanation: When men are involved, health choices and money are planned together, leading to a healthier family! Keep it up.

question: What is a major cause of family displacement and vulnerability across many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Conflict, banditry, and natural disasters
options.B: Mandatory retirement at age fifty
options.C: Too much funding from foreign donors
options.D: Government laws against farming

explanation: Correct! Insecurity and environmental challenges frequently displace Nigerian families, destroying their homes and traditional support systems.

question: Which body organ is mainly responsible for breaking down most oral cough medications?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Liver
options.C: Pancreas
options.D: Kidneys

explanation: The liver is our chemical processing plant—it breaks down oral drugs using special enzymes before the body clears them.

question: What is aeromicrobiology mainly about?

options.A: The measurement of atmospheric temperature and pressure
options.B: The study of living microbes floating in the air
options.C: The chemical composition of industrial smog
options.D: The treatment of chronic lung diseases in hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Aeromicrobiology simply looks at microorganisms that travel or hang out in the atmosphere for a bit. You've got this!

question: Why does a lack of mentorship often slow down research growth for young nurses?

options.A: Mentorship is illegal in most public Nigerian teaching hospitals
options.B: Experienced nurses prefer to keep research findings a secret
options.C: Experienced mentors charge expensive fees to teach data analysis
options.D: Young nurses miss out on guidance, confidence building, and practical support

explanation: Having a senior colleague to show you the ropes makes all the difference. Without guidance, new researchers often feel overwhelmed and give up. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of a School Health Programme?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic adult illnesses
options.B: To provide free accommodation for teachers
options.C: To replace local hospitals within rural communities
options.D: To promote and protect the well-being of students and staff

explanation: The core purpose of the programme is safeguarding the physical, mental, and social health of the school population. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T3#GNS225_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is the most effective way to prevent severe maternal distress during childbirth?

options.A: Providing continuous physical and emotional labor support
options.B: Isolating the mother to encourage quiet rest
options.C: Delaying pain relief until the second stage of labor
options.D: Restricting fluid intake throughout the entire first stage

explanation: Never underestimate the power of a caring nurse holding a hand and offering words of encouragement. Being present is the best medicine!

question: A mother says she mixed her child's ORS packet into half a liter of water instead of a full liter. What should you do?

options.A: Advise her to add extra sugar to balance out the high salt content
options.B: Instruct her to add another half-liter of water to the existing mixture and stir well
options.C: Allow her to feed the concentrated solution since it will work faster anyway
options.D: Discard the solution and help her mix a fresh batch correctly with one full liter of water

explanation: Guessing water amounts can throw off body chemistry. It is always safest to throw out the wrong mix and prepare a fresh, accurately measured batch.

question: What does the handy acronym AFASS help healthcare workers figure out about infant feeding?

options.A: The nutritional content of expressed breast milk
options.B: The rate of viral clearance in a nursing mother
options.C: The exact dosage of infant antiretroviral medications
options.D: The safety and suitability of replacement formula feeding

explanation: AFASS is a great tool! It checks if formula feeding is Affordable, Feasible, Acceptable, Sustainable, and Safe for the family's real-life situation.

question: What is the absolute first action a nurse expects when caring for a patient with serum sickness?

options.A: Stop administering the triggering medication
options.B: Start immediate daily kidney dialysis
options.C: Give a blood transfusion to replace red cells
options.D: Apply cool water compresses to the joints

explanation: Rule number one in pharmacology reactions: stop the offending drug immediately so no more immune complexes can form!

question: What is the main purpose of performing Leopold's maneuvers during an antenatal visit?

options.A: To check if the mother has a urinary tract infection
options.B: To determine fetal position, size, and presentation
options.C: To measure the exact amount of blood in the body
options.D: To find out when the baby will start walking

explanation: Leopold's maneuvers use gentle hand movements on the abdomen to feel how the baby is lying. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is the most common correctable physical cause of male infertility?

options.A: Varicocele
options.B: Testicular torsion
options.C: Klinefelter syndrome
options.D: Cryptorchidism

explanation: A varicocele is an enlarged set of veins in the scrotum that doctors can surgically repair to help restore normal fertility. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h3)

question: A patient is worried that eating fats will only make them gain weight. How can you best explain the good side of fats?

options.A: Fats replace water in cells during dehydration
options.B: Fats are the only nutrient that can build muscle tissue
options.C: Fats protect vital organs and help absorb certain vitamins
options.D: Fats prevent the breakdown of proteins into glucose

explanation: Well done! Dietary fats aren't just about storage; they insulate our organs and are essential for absorbing key vitamins like A, D, E, and K.

question: What primary farming challenge do mountainous regions usually face?

options.A: Absence of any sunlight during the year
options.B: Excessive flat land and too much rainfall
options.C: Constantly flooded river basins
options.D: Steep slopes and short growing seasons

explanation: High altitudes have rocky, steep land and shorter periods of warm weather, making it tough for crops to grow.

question: What is the primary function of a hospital journal club?

options.A: To help nurses read, discuss, and understand research articles together
options.B: To discipline nurses who make mistakes during procedures
options.C: To write brand new research papers for international publishing
options.D: To raise money for buying new ward equipment

explanation: Brilliant! Journal clubs are cozy, supportive spaces where we break down studies together so everyone can learn without feeling intimidated.

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of high potassium (hyperkalemia)?

options.A: Taking medications that hold onto potassium
options.B: Using a diuretic that causes potassium loss
options.C: Advanced chronic kidney disease
options.D: Breakdown of damaged muscle tissue

explanation: You nailed it! Potassium-wasting diuretics actually flush potassium out of the body, so they cause low potassium (hypokalemia) instead.

question: Which form of a drug molecule passes most easily across biological cell membranes?

options.A: Ionized
options.B: Conjugated
options.C: Unionized
options.D: Protein-bound

explanation: Unionized (un-charged) drug molecules are more fat-friendly (lipophilic), helping them slip smoothly across cell membranes.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical side effect of minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Impaired motor coordination
options.B: Excessive daytime drowsiness
options.C: Respiratory depression
options.D: Severe muscle rigidity and high fever

explanation: Severe muscle rigidity and high fever point to a rare reaction from major tranquilizers called neuroleptic malignant syndrome, not minor ones.

question: When does tertiary prevention come into play during the course of an illness?

options.A: Before any risk factors are present in the community
options.B: During routine health promotion and wellness talks
options.C: After disease and complications have already occurred
options.D: When conducting mass screening tests for healthy adults

explanation: Tertiary prevention steps in when a disease is already established, focusing on helping the patient recover and manage life.

question: Older adults often experience stiffer chest walls and weaker breathing muscles. What is the direct result of this?

options.A: Rapid expansion of lung capacity during exercise
options.B: Total elimination of carbon dioxide from the blood
options.C: Higher residual volume and reduced vital capacity
options.D: An immediate increase in total lung surface area

explanation: Think of it like an old rubber band—stiffer chest walls and weaker muscles mean older adults can't take as deep a breath, and they trap more air in their lungs (residual volume).

question: What happens during the process of opsonization?

options.A: Blood vessels constrict to stop the spread of an infection
options.B: Antibodies punch direct holes in the cell wall of a virus
options.C: Red blood cells are destroyed to release iron to the tissues
options.D: Pathogens are coated with antibodies to help phagocytes swallow them

explanation: Opsonization is basically tagging an enemy for easy spotting. It's like putting a handle on a pathogen so immune cells like macrophages can easily grab and engulf it!

question: Why is swelling of the kidney drainage system (hydronephrosis) more common on the right side during pregnancy?

options.A: The right renal artery has a higher pressure than the left.
options.B: The pregnant uterus tilts and compresses the right ureter more.
options.C: The right kidney is anatomically larger than the left kidney.
options.D: Progesterone receptors are concentrated only in the right ureter.

explanation: The growing uterus tends to lean to the right, putting extra pressure on the right ureter. Small details like this make you a sharp clinical nurse!

question: Which of these is NOT a standard rule when picking essential medicines?

options.A: Proven clinical effectiveness in human trials
options.B: Affordability for the target patient population
options.C: Safety compared to other choices
options.D: The aesthetic appeal of the product packaging

explanation: Correct! A pretty wrapper doesn't make a drug safer or more effective for our patients.

question: What is the main focus of client-centered drug administration?

options.A: Following hospital medication schedules without exception
options.B: Leaving medication management entirely to the doctor
options.C: Reducing the time nurses spend talking to patients
options.D: Treating the patient as an active partner in their care

explanation: Client-centered care values the patient's active participation in their own treatment plan rather than treating them as a passive recipient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h1)

question: What special enzyme do ringworm and other fungus types use to break into the outer skin layers?

options.A: Keratinase
options.B: Bradykinin
options.C: Collagenase
options.D: Histamine

explanation: Dermatophytic fungi release keratinase, an enzyme that literally digests the tough keratin protein found in your outer skin, hair, and nails.

question: Why do nurses regularly monitor a child's growth?

options.A: To calculate exact adult height and weight
options.B: To diagnose specific genetic disorders instantly
options.C: To catch health and nutritional problems early
options.D: To replace routine medical checkups entirely

explanation: You've got this! Growth monitoring helps us spot tiny changes or downward trends early on, long before a child gets seriously ill. It's a quick win for preventive care!

question: Which of these is an example of a macronutrient that the body needs in large amounts?

options.A: Trace minerals
options.B: Iron supplements
options.C: Vitamins
options.D: Carbohydrates

explanation: Correct! 'Macro' means big—carbs, proteins, and fats are the big-ticket items our bodies need daily in large quantities for fuel.

question: When breast cancer cells start to spread, where is the very first place they usually travel?

options.A: The main coronary artery system
options.B: The axillary lymph node network
options.C: The superficial jugular veins
options.D: The central spinal fluid pathway

explanation: The lymph fluid from the breast drains straight toward the armpit, making the axillary nodes the first station cancer cells visit on their spread.

question: What communication habit should a nurse avoid when explaining a new medication to a patient?

options.A: Using heavy medical jargon that the patient cannot easily follow
options.B: Encouraging the patient to speak up if they have any worries
options.C: Slowing down the conversation to match the client's pace
options.D: Asking open-ended questions about how they plan to take the pills

explanation: Complex medical terminology confuses patients and prevents them from truly understanding their treatment plan. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Regulating fluid balance and supporting nerve and muscle function
options.B: Acting as organic enzymes to speed up chemical digestion
options.C: Providing the structural framework for red blood cell hemoglobin
options.D: Serving as the body's primary emergency source of stored calories

explanation: Correct! Electrolytes like sodium and potassium keep our body fluids balanced and help our nerves and muscles work smoothly without cramping.

question: A patient living in a rural village needs regular blood pressure checks but cannot travel easily to the clinic. Which internet-based service is best suited for this situation?

options.A: Telehealth and remote monitoring
options.B: Offline hospital database backups
options.C: Standard paper filing systems
options.D: Internal local area network wiring

explanation: Telehealth bridges geographical gaps, allowing continuous care and observation for patients far away from the main hospital. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T9#GNS113_U1_T9_h4)

question: If an unresponsive patient is taking slow, gasping, irregular breaths, how should a nurse respond?

options.A: As an indication to wait for natural breathing to stabilize
options.B: As a sign that the patient is recovering normal oxygen levels
options.C: As agonal respirations requiring immediate start of CPR
options.D: As proof that the airway is clear and no further action is needed

explanation: Don't let those gasps fool you! Agonal gasps are just a reflex when the heart stops. Treat them as cardiac arrest and start CPR right away.

question: Research objectives need to be clear and measurable. What kind of words should they always start with?

options.A: Pronouns
options.B: Action verbs
options.C: Prepositions
options.D: Adjectives

explanation: Always kick off your objectives with active words like 'to evaluate', 'to assess', or 'to compare' so everyone knows exactly what you plan to do.

question: What is the main job of dietary calcium during the teenage years?

options.A: Enhancing visual acuity
options.B: Regulating blood pressure
options.C: Building peak bone mass
options.D: Preventing adult anemia

explanation: Spot on! The teenage years are the golden window where most of your adult bone strength is locked in. Drink up that milk!

question: What does active listening really mean when you are trying to negotiate for health changes?

options.A: Agreeing to all demands without questioning policies
options.B: Understanding the constraints and viewpoints of decision-makers
options.C: Taking notes only to prove the other party is wrong
options.D: Interrupting opponents to correct their facts quickly

explanation: That's right! When you listen to where decision-makers are coming from, it's much easier to find common ground and reach a good compromise.

question: What does a "double burden of disease" mean in Nigerian public health?

options.A: Having high rates of both maternal and child mortality simultaneously
options.B: Suffering from simultaneous outbreaks of waterborne and airborne infections
options.C: Managing high patient loads in both rural clinics and urban teaching hospitals
options.D: Dealing with both infectious diseases and chronic non-communicable diseases

explanation: Great job! A double burden simply means our healthcare system has to fight old enemies like malaria and TB while also managing the rising wave of lifestyle diseases like hypertension and diabetes.

question: Which type of estrogen is the strongest and most active during a woman's reproductive years?

options.A: Estriol
options.B: Estradiol
options.C: Estrone
options.D: Eplerenone

explanation: Estradiol is the heavy hitter! It's produced in the highest amounts by the ovaries and drives most estrogen activity before menopause.

question: A nurse is preparing to feed a patient via a PEG tube. What action should be performed first?

options.A: Flush the tube rapidly with 100 mL of cold water
options.B: Lie the patient completely flat to check the abdomen
options.C: Verify tube placement and assess bowel sounds
options.D: Attach the feeding bag and start the pump immediately

explanation: Safety checks like confirming tube position and ensuring active bowel sounds must always happen before introducing any fluid or formula. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T4#GNS212_U1_T4_h3)

question: A clinical trial claims a new bandage prevents infections, but later studies show it doesn't. What type of error happened?

options.A: Descriptive error
options.B: Type II error
options.C: Sampling error
options.D: Type I error

explanation: You nailed it! Believing an intervention works when it's actually useless is a classic false positive, which is a Type I error. Keep crushing it!

question: Which pancreatic hormone lowers blood sugar by helping cells take in glucose?

options.A: Glucagon
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Adrenaline
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Insulin acts as the primary hormone that allows body cells to absorb glucose from the bloodstream, thereby lowering blood sugar. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why can frequent use of high-strength spermicide sometimes increase the risk of infections?

options.A: It permanently paralyzes the immune cells in the bloodstream
options.B: It neutralizes all normal vaginal flora leaving the body dry
options.C: It can cause tiny cuts in vaginal tissue that let viruses enter
options.D: It reacts with air to create toxic gases inside the pelvis

explanation: That's right! Chemical irritation from overuse can break down natural tissue defenses, making it easier for infections to slip in.

question: Which of these is a common acquired (later in life) cause of a shortened fallopian tube?

options.A: Age-related natural hormonal decline
options.B: Previous partial salpingectomy or pelvic surgery
options.C: Frequent heavy physical exercise
options.D: Long-term use of oral contraceptive pills

explanation: If a part of the tube has to be surgically removed—like during treatment for an ectopic pregnancy—the overall length of the tube becomes shorter.

question: A patient handles ward stress by going for brisk walks and talking things through with a close friend. How would a nurse label this response?

options.A: Psychotic
options.B: Adaptive
options.C: Regressive
options.D: Maladaptive

explanation: Spot on! Exercising and leaning on a support system are classic healthy, adaptive ways to handle pressure.

question: Why do symptoms suddenly show up after a quiet incubation phase?

options.A: The number of germs and body damage cross a tipping point
options.B: The immune system completely stops working
options.C: The germs suddenly turn into a completely different species
options.D: Medicines taken by the patient start fighting healthy cells

explanation: Illness only becomes visible when the growing number of germs and tiny injuries finally overwhelm the body's natural defenses. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h2)

question: What is the name of the age-related muscle loss condition that often affects nutritional assessments in older adults?

options.A: Sarcopenia
options.B: Osteoporosis
options.C: Atherosclerosis
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Well done! Sarcopenia is the gradual, natural decrease in muscle mass and strength as people age, which changes what normal body composition looks like for them.

question: Why are ritual prayers and sacrifices often combined with herbal treatments in traditional care?

options.A: To replace the need for any form of human interaction
options.B: To confuse the patient and make them forget their personal problems
options.C: To address both the physical symptoms and the spiritual cause of the illness
options.D: To test the physical strength of the sick person

explanation: You got it! Because illness is viewed as multidimensional, treatments target both the physical body with herbs and the spiritual realm with rituals.

question: What is the primary function of the musculoskeletal system?

options.A: Filtering waste products from the bloodstream
options.B: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.C: Providing structural support and enabling movement
options.D: Regulating core body temperature through sweating

explanation: The primary roles of the musculoskeletal system are giving the body shape, protecting organs, and allowing physical movement through muscle contraction. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T1#GNS221_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does a genetic predisposition to a mental disorder mean?

options.A: The person will definitely develop the illness as they age
options.B: The illness cannot be treated with modern psychiatric medications
options.C: The condition was caused entirely by a poor diet in childhood
options.D: The person has a higher chance of developing the condition

explanation: Genetic predisposition means a person carries inherited vulnerabilities that make them more likely to develop a disorder if other triggers are present. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why are items like sugary soft drinks left out of standard food groups?

options.A: They are too expensive for rural families to buy
options.B: They contain too much water and zero calories
options.C: They spoil too quickly in warm tropical climates
options.D: They offer little to no real nutritional value

explanation: Exactly! Dietary scores focus on nutrient-packed foods that actually build health, rather than empty calories.

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing most routine vaccines in a clinic fridge?

options.A: Plus 15 degrees Celsius to plus 25 degrees Celsius
options.B: Minus 2 degrees Celsius to zero degrees Celsius
options.C: Plus 2 degrees Celsius to plus 8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Minus 15 degrees Celsius to minus 25 degrees Celsius

explanation: Keep this safe range in mind! +2°C to +8°C keeps most routine refrigerated vaccines cool and happy without freezing them.

question: Which famous nursing theorist built her work around the patient's ability to perform self-care?

options.A: Callista Roy
options.B: Florence Nightingale
options.C: Dorothea Orem
options.D: Madeleine Leininger

explanation: Correct! Dorothea Orem's Self-Care Deficit Theory focuses on stepping in to help patients when they cannot manage their own self-care.

question: What is the proper way to position an adult's ear before putting in ear drops?

options.A: Pull the pinna up and back before instilling the drops
options.B: Keep the client sitting upright for thirty minutes after
options.C: Insert the dropper tip firmly deep into the ear canal
options.D: Pull the earlobe straight down before putting in drops

explanation: Correct! Pulling the pinna up and back opens up the canal so the drops slide right down nicely toward the eardrum.

question: Which food source gives us iron that our bodies can absorb the easiest?

options.A: Inorganic iron found in mineral spring water
options.B: Heme iron found in animal products
options.C: Non-heme iron found in leafy green vegetables
options.D: Fortified iron found in refined white flour

explanation: You got it! Heme iron from meats, fish, and poultry is easily taken up by your body compared to plant sources.

question: What is 'diagnostic overshadowing' in clinical practice?

options.A: Physical symptoms being incorrectly dismissed as psychological issues
options.B: Family members refusing to accept any medical diagnosis
options.C: A patient receiving two different psychiatric labels at the exact same time
options.D: A clinician forgetting to document the patient's primary complaint

explanation: Overshadowing happens when real physical sickness gets ignored simply because the patient has a mental health history. Always look at the whole person!

question: A community health nurse notices many young people in her village developing untreated high blood pressure. What action best reflects modern primary health care nursing practice?

options.A: Waiting inside the urban teaching hospital for patients to travel and find her
options.B: Focusing solely on childhood immunizations and ignoring adult health entirely
options.C: Organizing a local screening camp combined with lifestyle and diet counseling
options.D: Telling the villagers that chronic illnesses cannot be managed at the local level

explanation: Proactive community screening and health education bring prevention and early management directly to the people, fulfilling PHC goals. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT normal and actually represents a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Passing dark green meconium poop on the first day
options.B: Grunting when breathing and chest sinking in
options.C: Spitting up a tiny bit of milk after feeding
options.D: Sleeping soundly between regular feeds

explanation: Chest retractions and grunting are red flags! They tell us the baby is working way too hard to breathe and needs urgent help.

question: Which type of research relies mostly on numbers and statistics?

options.A: Phenomenological research
options.B: Qualitative research
options.C: Ethnographic research
options.D: Quantitative research

explanation: You nailed it! Quantitative research deals with measurable variables and numbers to find clear patterns and test relationships. Think 'quant' for quantity and numbers! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the main job of red bone marrow?

options.A: Synthesizing the organic collagen matrix
options.B: Producing blood cells through hematopoiesis
options.C: Storing energy reserves as triglycerides
options.D: Releasing calcium ions directly into bone

explanation: Red marrow is our body's busy factory for making red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets. Excellent!

question: What is a helpful early nursing action for a survivor who is panicking right after a disaster?

options.A: Leaving the patient entirely alone in a dark room until they calm down
options.B: Telling them to stop crying because others have worse injuries
options.C: Offering calming reassurance, active listening, and simple factual information
options.D: Administering high-dose antipsychotic medications immediately

explanation: Well done! Psychological first aid is all about being present, listening calmly, and speaking gently to help bring someone back to a sense of safety.

question: What forms the numerator in the standard prevalence formula?

options.A: Total number of existing cases
options.B: Number of newly reported deaths
options.C: Number of people who recovered
options.D: Total population size at risk

explanation: The top part of the fraction always represents all existing cases, both old and new, at that moment. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h3)

question: What are the two opposite ends of the Illness-Wellness Continuum?

options.A: Physical weakness and mental strength
options.B: Acute infection and chronic disability
options.C: Hospital admission and complete recovery
options.D: Premature death and high-level wellness

explanation: The continuum ranges from death on the left to optimal wellness on the right. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T3#GNS112_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is it so important to find the root cause of a gap found during an audit?

options.A: To justify closing down the nursing department permanently
options.B: To make sure every single nurse on duty receives a formal warning
options.C: So the corrective action actually fixes the real underlying problem
options.D: To prove that the hospital administration has zero funds left

explanation: You nailed it! Finding the root cause ensures we fix the actual issue—whether it's a lack of training or a shortage of supplies—rather than just guessing.

question: Which blood test is more specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Lipase
options.C: Creatinine
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Spot on! Serum lipase is the go-to test because it's much more specific to the pancreas than amylase, and it stays elevated longer during an attack.

question: A community nurse advocating for marginalized groups during disaster planning is primarily trying to achieve what?

options.A: Speed up the building of commercial property in the area
options.B: Ensure vulnerable populations receive equal safety provisions
options.C: Reduce the total number of emergency personnel needed
options.D: Secure extra funding for hospital construction projects

explanation: Exactly! Advocacy ensures that groups who might struggle during an evacuation are fully cared for in safety plans.

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of growth faltering in infants?

options.A: Regular daily physical exercise
options.B: Frequent bouts of childhood diarrhea
options.C: Inadequate complementary feeding
options.D: Recurrent malarial infections

explanation: Normal baby movement doesn't cause faltering. Illness, infections, and poor feeding are the real culprits behind slowed growth.

question: A healthy toddler suddenly starts eating less food than before. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Growth velocity naturally slows down after infancy, reducing food demand
options.B: The child is entering a severe phase of permanent nutritional failure
options.C: Breast milk or formula is no longer needed in any form
options.D: The child has developed an irreversible eating disorder

explanation: Don't panic if a toddler's appetite dips! Because growth slows down after year one, they simply don't need as many calories per kilogram. It's completely normal.

question: What is a vital safety step when nursing a patient with Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Setting up fall precautions because of poor coordination
options.B: Encouraging heavy gym workouts to build leg strength
options.C: Restricting all fluids to stop brain swelling
options.D: Keeping the room pitch black all day

explanation: Spot on! Because these patients struggle with balance (ataxia), keeping them safe from nasty falls is a top nursing priority.

question: How is desiccated thyroid extract different from synthetic levothyroxine?

options.A: Both thyroxine and triiodothyronine from animal sources
options.B: Non-hormonal plant extracts that stimulate the pituitary
options.C: Only pure synthetic triiodothyronine
options.D: Chemically altered molecules designed to bypass the liver

explanation: Desiccated thyroid comes from dried animal glands, meaning it naturally carries a mix of thyroid hormones rather than just one lab-created formula.

question: Which maternal blood vessels are opened up by the placenta to bathe the fetal villi in nutrient-rich blood?

options.A: Cardinal veins
options.B: Uterine veins
options.C: Umbilical arteries
options.D: Spiral arteries

explanation: Spot on! The trophoblast gently remodels the mother's spiral arteries so that blood pools nicely around the baby's villi for easy sharing.

question: A patient turns yellowish and has severe upper belly pain after mixing local herbs with paracetamol for weeks. What likely happened?

options.A: Drug-induced liver injury from combined metabolic toxicity
options.B: A complete blockage of the urinary tract by solid crystals
options.C: Sudden infection caused by drinking too much cold water daily
options.D: A normal, expected side effect of taking harmless herbal teas

explanation: The liver has to process everything we swallow. Combining heavy doses of drugs and potent herbal mixes overworks the liver and can cause serious damage.

question: How do nursing leaders make sure a successful new practice becomes permanent?

options.A: Stop collecting data and assume staff will remember
options.B: Keep the new guidelines secret from managers
options.C: Punish any nurse who mentions the old way of doing things
options.D: Integrate the new steps into standard hospital policies and staff orientation

explanation: Spot on! Baking the new steps straight into official policies and student orientations ensures everyone learns the right way from day one.

question: What is the main difference in how a research objective and a research question are written?

options.A: A question uses medical jargon, while an objective uses everyday language
options.B: An objective is always a guess, while a question is a proven fact
options.C: An objective is written at the end of the study, while a question is written at the beginning
options.D: An objective is a declarative statement using an action verb, while a question is interrogative

explanation: Remember: an objective makes a statement using an action verb (like 'To determine...'), whereas a question asks something directly with a question mark at the end. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h3)

question: You just finished explaining how to mix oral rehydration salts to a father. What is the best next step?

options.A: Send him home immediately to start treatment without checking
options.B: Assume he understood because he nodded his head politely
options.C: Ask the father to demonstrate how he will mix the solution
options.D: Give him a written quiz with difficult multiple-choice questions

explanation: Spot on! Having him show you right away is the best practical way to ensure he really understood and can do it at home.

question: What is a key priority for a nurse when conducting a sexual health assessment with an adolescent?

options.A: Scolding the teenager for engaging in risky behaviors
options.B: Focusing solely on physical vitals while ignoring mental health
options.C: Ensuring confidentiality and building a trusting relationship
options.D: Reporting every detail immediately to the school principal

explanation: Teens will only share honest information about their sexual health if they trust the nurse and know their secrets are safe. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h9)

question: Which of these statements is actually FALSE regarding histograms and ogives?

options.A: A histogram is used exclusively for qualitative categories rather than numerical data
options.B: An ogive can be used to find medians visually whereas a histogram cannot do this easily
options.C: An ogive displays running cumulative totals while a histogram shows single group frequencies
options.D: A histogram uses bars while an ogive uses connected points to form a polygon

explanation: You nailed it! Both histograms and ogives are meant for numerical data—histograms use bars for separate groups, while ogives use connected points for running totals.

question: Which of the following is an example of a descriptive statistic?

options.A: A surgical success prediction model
options.B: The exact biological cause of a virus mutation
options.C: A proven cure rate for a genetic disorder
options.D: Percentage of patients with high blood pressure

explanation: Numbers like percentages, averages, and counts are classic descriptive statistics that simply summarize what is happening in the data. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h6)

question: What makes a hybrid computer special?

options.A: It can only function inside a hospital operating theatre
options.B: It combines the input and output features of both analog and digital systems
options.C: It relies entirely on manual data entry without electricity
options.D: It operates without a central processing unit

explanation: Think of hybrid as the best of both worlds! It takes continuous physical signals and turns them into digital numbers so we can process them easily.

question: Why is teaching the community so important for getting rid of infection reservoirs long-term?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any professional medical personnel
options.B: It empowers local residents to sustain hygiene and sanitation practices independently
options.C: It replaces the scientific need for laboratory testing and animal vaccines
options.D: It ensures that infectious pathogens mutate into harmless environmental plants

explanation: When people understand the 'why' behind healthy habits, they keep practicing good hygiene long after healthcare workers pack up and leave. Community power!

question: Why must honey be strictly avoided for infants under one year of age?

options.A: It contains high levels of artificial food coloring
options.B: It always causes immediate childhood obesity
options.C: It carries a severe risk of causing infant botulism
options.D: It replaces the need for essential milk feeds

explanation: Honey can contain spores of the bacterium Clostridium botulinum, which immature infant digestive tracts cannot fight off safely. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h4)

question: You are posted to a rural village where women have closely spaced pregnancies. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Advise community leaders to ban all marriages for young women
options.B: Wait for patients to visit the hospital before discussing reproductive health
options.C: Organize community education on birth spacing and offer family planning counseling
options.D: Focus all clinic resources exclusively on geriatric care programs

explanation: Fantastic! Taking education directly to the community helps families learn about safe birth spacing and maternal health.

question: Why do we use a Gram stain when looking at a bacterial colony under the microscope?

options.A: To measure the exact weight of the bacterial sample on a scale
options.B: To freeze the microorganisms so they can be stored for years
options.C: To provide extra nutrients for the bacteria to grow faster
options.D: To categorize the bacteria by their cell wall structure and color

explanation: Gram staining is a classic nursing and lab trick! It sorts bacteria into neat groups based on how their cell walls react to the violet dye.

question: Which layer of the uterus gives it the strong power to push out a baby during labor?

options.A: Perimetrium
options.B: Epimetrium
options.C: Myometrium
options.D: Endometrium

explanation: Well done! The myometrium is made of thick, strong muscle that contracts powerfully during childbirth.

question: Why must pregnant women attend antenatal clinics even when they feel completely fine?

options.A: To eliminate all potential discomforts of pregnancy
options.B: To prevent the fetus from moving into a breech position
options.C: To detect silent conditions like high blood pressure early
options.D: To guarantee a normal vaginal delivery date

explanation: You got it! Some dangerous issues like high blood pressure don't show early signs, which is why regular clinic checks are so important.

question: Which of these tasks is the main job of the scrub nurse during an operation?

options.A: Positioning the operating table and adjusting surgical lights
options.B: Tracking sponge counts and handing instruments to the surgeon
options.C: Managing patient billing and specimen transport logistics
options.D: Completing the electronic health record and nursing notes

explanation: The scrub nurse stays sterile right at the field, passing tools smoothly and keeping a careful count of sponges and instruments.

question: Why is having a chain of command (hierarchical system) for hormones helpful for the body?

options.A: It prevents any possibility of hormone overproduction or toxicity
options.B: It allows a central brain region to coordinate widespread body responses
options.C: It eliminates the need for negative feedback loops in peripheral organs
options.D: It ensures that blood glucose levels remain entirely independent of brain activity

explanation: Having the brain act as the head office allows it to smoothly manage and coordinate multiple glands all over the body at once.

question: How do mast cell stabilizers stop allergic symptoms from starting?

options.A: By directly destroying free-floating allergen particles
options.B: By permanently shrinking the size of mucous glands
options.C: By replacing natural antibodies in the bloodstream
options.D: By stopping mast cells from bursting and releasing histamine

explanation: You nailed it! They act like strong shields, keeping mast cell walls intact so the histamine inside cannot escape to cause trouble.

question: In basic terms, what is a poison?

options.A: Any substance that disrupts body functions or causes harm when introduced
options.B: A prescription drug taken strictly according to doctor instructions
options.C: A chemical compound that only harms the liver and kidneys
options.D: An infectious microorganism found in contaminated water sources

explanation: Spot on! A poison is simply anything that enters the body and causes harm or upsets normal body functions. You've got this!

question: How does cognitivism view how our minds handle learning?

options.A: As an emotional center completely separate from memory
options.B: As an active information processor similar to a computer
options.C: As a blank slate that only reacts to external rewards
options.D: As a muscle that only grows through physical exercise

explanation: Think of your brain like a smart computer: it takes in data, processes it, stores it safely, and pulls it back out when you need it on the ward.

question: What is the main job of the pudendal nerve in urinary control?

options.A: It automatically relaxes the detrusor muscle.
options.B: It gives you conscious control over the outer urinary sphincter.
options.C: It senses spasms in the upper ureters.
options.D: It tells the kidneys to make more urine.

explanation: Fantastic! The pudendal nerve lets you consciously decide when to tighten or relax your external sphincter—saving you from accidents in class!

question: Why is it a bad idea to use straight, unconditioned ice packs when packing a vaccine carrier?

options.A: It creates an unpleasant smell inside the carrier
options.B: It prevents the lid from closing tightly
options.C: It can freeze and ruin sensitive vaccines
options.D: It will melt too fast and flood the container

explanation: Unconditioned ice packs are bone-chillingly cold and can instantly freeze your vaccines on contact. Always let them sweat or 'condition' a bit first!

question: What often happens to ongoing health programs in Nigeria when a new political administration takes over?

options.A: Complete elimination of the federal ministry of health
options.B: Automatic privatization of all public teaching hospitals
options.C: Immediate reduction of nurse salaries nationwide
options.D: Disruption of ongoing health projects due to changing agendas

explanation: Spot on! New leaders often drop old projects to focus on their own fresh ideas, which can sadly slow down long-term progress in the health sector.

question: A newly opened nursing home focuses entirely on packing in as many residents as possible to maximize government payouts. Based on trends from the 1960s and 70s, what is a likely result?

options.A: Excessive funding directly spent on recreational programs
options.B: Compromised quality of resident care and severe staff burnout
options.C: Immediate elimination of all chronic health conditions
options.D: Universal praise from visiting public health inspectors

explanation: When a facility chases high numbers over quality care, they usually cut corners on staffing. This leaves nurses overworked and patients getting less-than-ideal attention.

question: A 10-month-old cannot sit unsupported, keeps fists clenched, and has stiff legs that cross like scissors when lifted. What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal infant development
options.B: A mild viral ear infection
options.C: Cerebral palsy
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Delayed sitting, tight fists, and scissoring legs are classic signs that point towards cerebral palsy during developmental checks.

question: Which condition is a speech-language pathologist specially trained to evaluate and treat?

options.A: Dysphagia
options.B: Contractures
options.C: Spasticity
options.D: Osteoporosis

explanation: Dysphagia is the medical term for swallowing difficulty. Speech therapists evaluate this carefully to prevent choking and lung infections.

question: Which group in the community is usually hit hardest by nutritional food taboos?

options.A: Young adult working males
options.B: Pregnant and lactating women
options.C: Unmarried teenage boys
options.D: Elderly male community leaders

explanation: Expectant and breastfeeding mothers need extra nutrition, which unfortunately makes them prime targets for restrictive cultural rules.

question: What is a big plus of using hydrogen peroxide gas plasma compared to older gas methods?

options.A: It works instantly without needing any special packaging
options.B: It can be performed easily using standard washbasins
options.C: It operates at low temperatures and leaves no toxic residue
options.D: It is the cheapest method available for hospital wards

explanation: Gas plasma is gentle on delicate equipment and breaks down into harmless water and oxygen, skipping the long wait for aeration.

question: As a psychiatric nurse, how should you view a patient's mental health symptoms when you first meet them?

options.A: As deliberate choices made to upset family members
options.B: As proof that the patient lacks all willpower
options.C: As an attempt by the psyche to protect itself
options.D: As permanent brain damage that cannot heal

explanation: Every symptom has a backstory. When we view symptoms as the mind's clumsy way of shielding itself from pain, it becomes much easier to care for our patients without judgment.

question: Which of the following is an example of an adaptive coping mechanism for a newly diagnosed HIV patient?

options.A: Turning to heavy alcohol use to forget the diagnosis
options.B: Denying the existence of the virus and skipping clinic visits
options.C: Joining a peer support group and talking with a counsellor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from all human contact

explanation: Seeking community support and professional guidance helps patients process their diagnosis in a healthy, constructive manner. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: Which chemical builds up in your brain throughout the day to make you feel sleepy?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Adenosine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Adenosine piles up the longer you stay awake, creating sleep pressure until you finally rest and clear it out.

question: Why is it so helpful to link diagnostic results directly into the Electronic Health Record (EHR)?

options.A: It prevents patients from ever seeing their own medical information
options.B: It automatically cures the patient without requiring nurse intervention
options.C: It stops diagnostic machines from breaking down over time
options.D: It allows healthcare providers to view test results and images in one central place

explanation: Having everything in one digital spot helps the whole care team make quick, safe decisions without chasing paper files!

question: What marks the biological beginning of the adolescent period?

options.A: Reaching legal majority age
options.B: The onset of puberty
options.C: Complete physical growth stopping
options.D: Entering secondary school

explanation: Puberty triggers the physical and hormonal changes that officially mark the entry into adolescence. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which symptom do pregnant women often report along with constipation?

options.A: Sudden loss of all body hair
options.B: Constant swelling of the eyelids
options.C: Abdominal bloating and cramping
options.D: Inability to hear high-pitched sounds

explanation: Correct! When gas and waste move slowly through the large bowel, it naturally leads to uncomfortable bloating and mild cramps.

question: Why is women empowerment considered essential for achieving universal health coverage?

options.A: It stops the government from building more primary health centers
options.B: It allows women to actively participate in seeking and utilizing healthcare services
options.C: It completely removes the financial cost of purchasing hospital drugs
options.D: It guarantees that only female doctors will treat patients

explanation: When women have autonomy, they can freely access health facilities and make prompt decisions that improve community health indices. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T59#GNS214_U1_T59_h1)

question: A student proposes to study 'every health issue affecting every patient in the country.' What is the main problem with this topic?

options.A: The methodology uses too many statistical tests
options.B: It focuses too much on ethical patient consent
options.C: It relies entirely on recent nursing journals
options.D: The scope is far too broad to be manageable

explanation: A good proposal needs a narrow, focused topic so you can actually finish it successfully without getting overwhelmed!

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about dominant genetic disorders that nurses often correct?

options.A: Lifestyle changes can completely erase a faulty gene
options.B: Genetic conditions never show up in families twice
options.C: Every child of an affected parent will automatically inherit the disease
options.D: Genetic disorders only affect elderly individuals

explanation: With autosomal dominant conditions, each pregnancy carries a specific probability, such as fifty percent, rather than an absolute certainty for every single child. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T20#GNS222_U4_T20_h3)

question: What is an exciting potential use of augmented reality (AR) glasses in nursing care?

options.A: Projecting vital signs and vein maps directly into the nurse's view
options.B: Automatically administering medications through wireless signals
options.C: Replacing the need for physical nursing assessments entirely
options.D: Printing paper charts without needing ink or toner cartridges

explanation: How cool is that? AR glasses overlay helpful digital patient data and vein guides right into your natural field of vision while you work.

question: Why is it a mistake for a nurse manager to panic over every single normal, everyday variation?

options.A: It causes the hospital to lose its government license.
options.B: It creates unnecessary panic and wastes effort trying to fix a process that is working normally.
options.C: It forces staff to stop checking vital signs.
options.D: It instantly stops all new patient admissions to the ward.

explanation: Every day won't look identical. Overreacting to normal day-to-day fluctuations just stresses out the team for no reason!

question: A patient on a tight budget wants a cheap, local source of protein. What should you recommend?

options.A: Imported salmon fillets
options.B: Processed energy drinks
options.C: Beans and cowpeas
options.D: Refined white sugar

explanation: Local beans and cowpeas are fantastic, pocket-friendly powerhouses of plant-based protein right here in Nigeria!

question: How is child trafficking different from regular help on a family farm?

options.A: Trafficking always involves coercion and exploitation
options.B: Trafficking only happens in urban city centers
options.C: Normal labor is strictly illegal for all minors
options.D: Normal labor pays a much higher daily wage

explanation: While helping out with family chores or learning a trade can be safe, trafficking relies on deceit, force, and taking advantage of a child against their will.

question: Why is quick-freezing generally better for food quality than slow freezing?

options.A: It changes the food into a warm, cooked meal instantly
options.B: It forms tiny ice crystals that protect the food's cellular structure
options.C: It completely removes the need for any electricity or freezers
options.D: It adds extra sodium to keep the food tender

explanation: Quick-freezing prevents giant, sharp ice crystals from forming, meaning the delicate cell walls of the food stay intact and taste better later!

question: During the rainy season, a community health nurse sees more waterborne illnesses. What is the best immediate community action to prioritize?

options.A: Encouraging families to sleep under insecticide-treated bed nets every night
options.B: Advising community members to avoid all physical contact during greetings
options.C: Promoting daily physical exercise to strengthen cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Educating residents on water purification methods like boiling or chlorination

explanation: You got it! Since waterborne diseases spread through contaminated drinking water, making the water safe to drink is the most direct way to stop them.

question: A nurse hands a patient their morning pills, but the patient is busy talking on the phone and asks the nurse to leave the cup on the bedside table. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Place the pills in the patient's water cup so they dissolve for later
options.B: Take the pills away and document that the patient refused the medication
options.C: Leave the pills on the table and remind the nurse's assistant to check later
options.D: Stay with the patient, wait until they finish the call, and watch them take the pills

explanation: Medications should never be left unattended at the bedside because the patient might forget them, take them incorrectly, or someone else might take them. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T2#GNS122_U1_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge facing CBR implementation in Nigeria?

options.A: Widespread stigma and reliance on traditional healing homes
options.B: Severe shortage of trained mental health personnel at the primary care level
options.C: Excessive government funding and oversupply of psychiatric nurses in rural areas
options.D: Poor infrastructure and difficult rural road networks

explanation: Nigeria actually suffers from severe underfunding and a massive shortage of mental health professionals, making the first option completely false. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following is a major risk when electronic health record systems experience sudden downtime?

options.A: All medication pumps stop working simultaneously
options.B: Staff must revert to paper charting, which can increase transcription errors
options.C: Hospital doors automatically lock to prevent patient entry
options.D: Patient vital signs automatically delete themselves from memory

explanation: System downtime forces a return to manual paper records, raising the chance of mistakes during handovers and order transcription. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h7)

question: What makes a saturated fatty acid different from an unsaturated fatty acid?

options.A: Saturated fats lack any hydrogen atoms along the carbon chain
options.B: Saturated fats contain only single carbon-to-carbon bonds
options.C: Saturated fats contain multiple carbon-to-carbon double bonds
options.D: Saturated fats always dissolve easily in plain water

explanation: Because they only have single bonds, saturated fat molecules pack tightly together, which is why they are usually solid at room temperature.

question: What is the mandatory retirement age for public servants in the Nigerian civil service?

options.A: 60 years
options.B: 70 years
options.C: 50 years
options.D: 65 years

explanation: In the Nigerian civil service, the rule is to retire at 60 years of age or after 35 years of active service—whichever comes first!

question: Why are long-acting injectable (LAI) medications often preferred for patients on psychiatric parole?

options.A: They have zero side effects compared to oral tablets.
options.B: They save patients from having to remember daily pills.
options.C: They can be given safely without any medical training.
options.D: They completely cure chronic psychiatric disorders overnight.

explanation: Brilliant! LAIs keep steady drug levels in the body over weeks, solving the everyday struggle of missing daily pills.

question: In infection control, what does the latent period actually measure?

options.A: The time until clinical symptoms appear
options.B: The time until the person can transmit the pathogen
options.C: The total duration of hospital confinement
options.D: The time required for complete antibody clearance

explanation: Spot on! The latent period is the time it takes from catching the bug to actually becoming contagious to others.

question: For weak, frail patients, why do we recommend small, frequent meals instead of three big ones?

options.A: They prevent the patient from feeling overwhelmed and reduce fatigue during eating.
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for any fiber in the diet.
options.C: They stop the stomach from producing normal digestive acids.
options.D: They guarantee that the patient will consume twice as many calories.

explanation: Eating a huge plate of food can exhaust a frail patient. Smaller, tasty portions throughout the day make eating feel manageable and less tiring.

question: Which sanitation practice helps stop rats and mice from taking over residential areas?

options.A: Storing harvested grains directly on bare dirt floors inside homes
options.B: Properly covering refuse bins and clearing overgrown bushes
options.C: Leaving domestic food waste uncovered in open backyard spaces
options.D: Digging shallow soakaway pits close to kitchen entrances

explanation: Spot on! Covering trash cuts off their food supply, and clearing bushes takes away their hiding spots.

question: What does the 'double burden of malnutrition' mean in growing cities?

options.A: Suffering from two different strains of malaria at once
options.B: Having to pay double the price for imported rice
options.C: The presence of both childhood stunting and adult obesity
options.D: Carrying heavy water buckets over long distances

explanation: City environments can sometimes show both sides of the coin: undernutrition in young children and weight-related health issues in adults.

question: Why is breaking a massive problem down into tiny, bite-sized steps so helpful for an anxious patient?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further nursing interaction
options.B: It guarantees that all hospital bills will be paid instantly
options.C: It proves to the doctor that the patient is fully cured
options.D: It restores a sense of personal control and reduces panic

explanation: Well reasoned! Big problems can make anyone freeze up. Small steps make the climb feel possible again and calm the nerves.

question: A patient scheduled for parole review keeps refusing meds and denies being sick. What should the team do first?

options.A: Approve the release immediately to encourage independence.
options.B: Delay the release until their insight and compliance improve.
options.C: Ignore the medication refusal since it is a minor issue.
options.D: Discharge the patient with no follow-up requirements.

explanation: Safety first! Refusing medication and lacking insight are big warning signs that a patient isn't quite ready for independent community living yet.

question: What receptor combination is the trademark of second-generation (atypical) antipsychotics?

options.A: Dopamine and serotonin receptor blockade
options.B: Opioid and adrenergic receptor agonism
options.C: GABA and norepinephrine enhancement
options.D: Histamine and acetylcholine stimulation

explanation: Remember: first-gen mostly blocks dopamine, but second-gen (atypical) agents block both dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors at the same time.

question: Which method is best for reaching a large, scattered rural population across multiple villages at the same time?

options.A: A written textbook distributed to homes
options.B: Radio broadcast jingles
options.C: A silent demonstration with no sound
options.D: Individual bedside whispered counseling

explanation: Correct! Radio is a fantastic mass media tool to share quick health tips with people in areas you cannot visit every day.

question: When summarizing key results for a study on preventing pressure sores, what belongs right at the start?

options.A: Detailed instructions on how to use turning sheets
options.B: A complete list of every patient's medical history
options.C: Raw survey responses from all participating nurses
options.D: The main answer to the primary research question

explanation: You're crushing it! Always address the main question first so your reader immediately knows what the study found.

question: What is the main purpose of nursing research informatics?

options.A: Managing daily staff shift rosters and nurse-to-patient ratios
options.B: Supporting data collection and analysis to discover new nursing knowledge
options.C: Ordering routine hospital supplies and medical equipment inventory
options.D: Providing health tips and reminders to patients via mobile phones

explanation: Research informatics uses technology to manage studies, analyze data, and build the evidence base for nursing practice. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is patient coercion a serious worry during research recruitment?

options.A: Ethical boards do not allow patients to receive free medication
options.B: Coerced patients always give false answers on questionnaires
options.C: Patients might feel forced to join because their nurse or doctor asked
options.D: Hospital management requires a 100 percent recruitment rate

explanation: Brilliant! Patients respect their nurses and doctors so much that they might fear getting bad care if they say 'no,' which makes true voluntary consent tricky.

question: What is the primary physiological problem in clinical shock?

options.A: Inadequate blood flow and oxygen to tissues
options.B: An excessive buildup of red blood cells
options.C: A sudden drop in core body temperature
options.D: Severe localized pain in the chest

explanation: Shock happens when the circulatory system fails to deliver enough blood and oxygen to meet the basic needs of body tissues. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T2#GNS221_U3_T2_h1)

question: How do collected incident reports directly help improve hospital quality?

options.A: By ensuring the hospital meets strict interior cleaning schedules
options.B: By providing evidence to lower the salaries of underperforming staff
options.C: By revealing recurring error trends that guide workflow changes
options.D: By allowing administrators to reduce the number of working nurses

explanation: Spot on! Reviewing multiple reports together highlights patterns, helping managers fix root problems across the whole hospital.

question: What does medication adherence mean in daily nursing practice?

options.A: How closely a patient follows their prescribed treatment plan
options.B: The ability of a doctor to write clear prescriptions
options.C: The speed at which a drug is absorbed into the bloodstream
options.D: How strictly a pharmacy records daily drug sales

explanation: Adherence measures whether a patient takes their medications correctly regarding timing, dosage, and frequency as agreed upon with their healthcare provider. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which Nigerian agency is responsible for enforcing environmental rules, including safe hospital waste disposal?

options.A: National football federation
options.B: Agricultural research council
options.C: NESREA
options.D: Federal road safety commission

explanation: NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) is the body that makes sure hospitals and businesses manage their waste safely in Nigeria.

question: Why do clinicians love checking serum ferritin during a nutritional check-up?

options.A: It directly measures the body's stored iron reserves.
options.B: It calculates the total volume of circulating blood cells.
options.C: It tracks short-term protein intake over forty-eight hours.
options.D: It measures the exact amount of circulating vitamin C.

explanation: Ferritin gives you a sneak peek at how much iron the body has tucked away safely in reserve, long before actual anemia shows up.

question: What is the single most important thing a nurse can do to stop infections from spreading?

options.A: Performing thorough hand hygiene
options.B: Administering daily multivitamins
options.C: Keeping all windows wide open
options.D: Changing bed sheets once a week

explanation: Never underestimate good handwashing! It is our #1 weapon as nurses against hospital-acquired infections.

question: What does a line that slopes upward on a healthcare chart tell you?

options.A: An increase in the measured value over time
options.B: An error in drawing the horizontal axis
options.C: A drop in patient admissions to zero
options.D: A complete halt in all clinical data collection

explanation: Correct! An upward slope means your numbers are climbing higher as time moves forward.

question: What should a nurse manager do if they check the results and realize a new decision isn't working out?

options.A: Permanently stop evaluating all ward outcomes
options.B: Ignore the data and pretend everything is fine
options.C: Tweak the approach or pivot to a new strategy
options.D: Blame the junior nursing staff for sabotage

explanation: Evaluation is there to guide you. If a strategy falls short, a great leader adjusts their sails rather than ignoring reality.

question: What size of IV catheter is preferred for fast fluid replacement in a severe trauma patient?

options.A: Midline catheter with dual lumens
options.B: Large-bore catheter like 16 or 18 gauge
options.C: Small-bore catheter like 24 gauge
